utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good, everybody. Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good morning to you. Mr. Oric, I just want to make sure that you are receiving interpretation as usual in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, distinguished gentlemen, good morning. Yes, I am receiving interpretation into my language and I can follow the proceedings. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning my learned friends from the Defence team. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution, together with Jose Doria as counsel, and Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink as our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I am Vasvija Vidovic, together with Mr. John Jones, appearing for Mr. Naser Oric. Together with us our legal assistant Jasmina Cosic and our case manager, Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you, Madam, and your team. Any preliminaries before we bring in the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just one, Your Honour. We received the Prosecution response to our motion regarding authenticity and Rule 68 disclosure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't read it. I have it. I just got it on my desk, but I haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It's just to say that we wish to seek leave to file a reply, and under Rule 126 bis, it appears that could be -- leave could be sought either orally or in writing. I propose to seek your leave orally just because obviously it saves some time and resources in making a written application. And it might -- it would save the Prosecution possibly also fulfilling the need to reply a response to our application for leave and it goes on and on. The basis, briefly, would be that the Prosecution response refers to the testimony of Ms. Manas and that obviously came after we filed our motion and so that raises matters which we would like to reply to. So that's the basis for our application. And also the Sokolac CD index we received after -- we found after filing our motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. As I start, would you have an objection to the Defence filing a reply to your response?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I said, I haven't read it. I don't know if my colleagues have read it. My idea is to reserve our decision until after the break, in the meantime we will have seen it, we will consult, and we will take into consideration what you have said and of course there is no objection on the part of the Prosecution, and we'll probably come with a positive reaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: After the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I don't promise it obviously because we may not -- we haven't seen it, so we have to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, naturally.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mitrovic. And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Good morning, Mr. Mitrovic, and welcome back. Today as you see we tried to not lose time and to have you escorted into the courtroom as quickly as possible so that we try and start and hopefully finish. I won't promise you that we will finish today, I don't know, but it is possible. We'll try. If we don't, we will continue tomorrow and you will certainly finish tomorrow. You are going to give evidence very soon, and our rules require that before you do so you make a solemn declaration. That's -- would be equivalent to an oath, tantamount to the following, that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration is contained in a piece of paper that Madam Usher is going to hand to you now. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are a student. What are you studying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was a student when I gave the statement. That's why it's written in the statement that I'm enrolled in a school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What are you doing now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From time to time I work in the construction business, whatever job I can find.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. The procedure here is a very simple one, and I'm trying -- going to try and explain it to you. You will first be asked a series of questions by Mr. Wubben and -- who is representing the Prosecution here; he is the lead counsel. He will then be followed by Mr. Jones, who is one of the lawyers defending Naser Oric. In accordance with the solemn declaration that you have made, your duty is to answer all questions truthfully and fully, irrespective of who's putting them to you. In other words, you do not distinguish between questions coming from the Prosecution, because it's the Prosecution that have summoned you here, and questions from the Defence. You treat them the same; that is your responsibility. You are a witness of the Tribunal now, a witness of the court, and your duty is towards justice and truth. Do you -- have I made myself clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So, Mr. Wubben, I leave him in your hands. You can -- with regard to the preliminaries, you can go ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. I will start with my questions now. First question is related to your personal background. Your name is Branimir Mitrovic?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your nickname is Branko?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it -- one moment, is it Branko or Uki?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Branko is the name they refer to me while I was imprisoned, and Uki is the name I got after the exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is your date of birth the 1st May of 1985? I can't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You were born in Bajina Basta in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your ethnic origin is Serbian?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You are educated as a waiter? I can't hear you. Will you please speak up loud for the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And speak into the microphones, please, because otherwise we won't -- there are interpreters behind you that have to translate what you say into English and into French. So please try to help us. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let me take you back to the beginning of January 1993. You were living in Serbia in Bajina Basta?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: With your family?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were taken that month - so that's January, beginning January 1993 - by your uncle from Serbia to another place?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What's the name of that place?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: It was Zarkovici village, formerly known as Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And when was that, what date?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And where were you taken to my your uncle?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean where?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: To what place were you taken. You were brought to a house, a building or...

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: He took me to his house in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were your -- were you taken as well to your grandparents?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is the name of your grandmother Ivanka Mitrovic?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And the name of your grandfather Vidoje Mitrovic?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And were you taken to the house of your grandparents?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you stay the night in the house of your grandparents?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's where I spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what happened the day after the date of your arrival when you stayed in the house of your grandparents. You arrived on the 15th of January, you told the Judges. What happened on the 16th of January?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: On the 16th, in the morning, my grandmother woke me, or rather I woke up myself hearing shooting. I had no idea what was going on. I thought it could be the neighbours because it was their family saints day, and I thought they were shooting in the air. Anyway, my grandmother took me to the basement of the new house next to the old house where I had spent the night. And when I entered that house I stood in the doorway with a view of the meadows outside the village. I was lucky at that moment because a bullet came and hit the floor right between my feet. After that, my grandmother grabbed me and took me to the other end of that room inside the house to hide me behind a cupboard. We spent some time hiding behind the cupboard. And after that my grandmother took me by the hand and took me out of the house. As we were leaving, I noticed a man on the terrace of that new house. The man was dressed in a camouflage uniform. He didn't say anything. He just looked at us. My grandmother took me to a basement elsewhere in the village, the basement of an old house that had not been in use for years at the time. So we entered the basement and stayed there for a while. There was a little window next to the door through which I could look outside. My grandmother looked as well. I could see men in camouflage uniforms, that is soldiers, some of them wore berets, some of them wore red ribbons. I thought that they were Serb soldiers because of those berets and red ribbons, but my grandmother put me right. After a while, the shooting was still going on outside, and a man knocked on our door and opened. My grandmother was standing by the window at that moment. He asked if there was anybody else in there besides her, and she said there was me, her grandson. He had hand grenades around his belt. He was bearded, a large, big man. He said, You are under arrest. You have to come with us to Srebrenica. So we followed him. We had no choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: One moment, please. May I stop you there. When you took hide in that basement together with your grandparents, did your grandparents or you have any weapons with you?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry I didn't mention that. In that basement with us was our grandfather -- my grandfather who had a rifle, but he wasn't using it and he wasn't able to use it. It was just hanging there on a hook, but it wasn't an operational rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What happened with that rifle? Did you know or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: The rifle remained there after we were arrested. When we were arrested, the grandfather wasn't because he was hiding behind the door, so they didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next question is: Was your grandfather a kind of soldier or a guard or not; do you know?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I think he was a civilian because he was already old.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did he wear civilian clothes or did he wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The yes is referring to what, a uniform or civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: He was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My next question is related to this man that knocked on the door and asked your grandmother who were in. Can you describe this person further. You spoke about hand grenades. Let me first with --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had hand grenades on his belt. He also had an automatic rifle. In his hand he was carrying a Motorola. I learned later it was a Motorola, but I could recognise it for a radio device even then. He had dark hair. He was wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: A military uniform? When you --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I said a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And he was wearing an automatic rifle. Can you describe that further or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: All I know was that it was an automatic rifle -- that bears distinction that I could make. I could distinguish an automatic rifle from the kind that my grandfather had. I didn't know at the time any specific types of rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So your grandmother was then referring to you. And what happened? I will rephrase my question, sorry. Your grandmother confirmed to this man that you were also there, and what happened then after this?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: The man said that we were under arrest and that we had to follow him, that we were going to Srebrenica. Until then -- as I child I had never heard of Srebrenica before. It was a totally unknown concept to me. And when he said we were under arrest, I realised what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When you took a look at that man, he was a soldier, military man? Did he have -- yes? Can you confirm that or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he's already answered you that he was wearing a camouflage uniform, so -- carrying an automatic gun with hand grenades around his belt. I mean, what else do you expect?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So this man was a soldier?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Was this man a Serbian soldier or a man from another ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: As soon as he said, You are under arrest, I knew that he was not of the same ethnicity as we. Things became clear the moment he said, You are under arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So -- what ethnicity he was? Did you find out? Was this a Croatian or a Muslim or another Serb, as you told the Court?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I learned later in Srebrenica after my arrest, I learned from talking to various people about my arrest - I didn't learn for certain - but I learned that it was Naser Oric. I said it in my statement. That's the most I could find out, based on the stories I heard from Muslim people during my detention in Srebrenica before I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, my next question will be: This man referred to as Naser Oric, did he wear also a belt or a ribbon around his head like the other soldiers you noticed around in Skelani upon your arrest?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember really now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What did you notice when you left this basement after your arrest by this person referred to as Naser Oric? Where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: We were taken towards the exit from the village. As we were walking, next to us was the house of a neighbour who was celebrating this saints day, St. John Day. And there were people in civilian clothes sitting there drinking and eating the food and the drink that had been prepared for the celebration. So we passed by those people, and we emerged on a meadow where we found more Serb people who had been arrested. There were also more soldiers, armed soldiers. When we arrived there, a soldier gave me his hand and hid me in a ditch to save me from being shot because the shooting was going on. My grandmother was begging all the time that they let me go; however, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When you saw these soldiers around during that shooting and taking subsequently to your arrest -- to another place, these soldiers were Muslim soldiers or from another ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that much is certain. I am certain about that because there were a number of other women from the village, too. That was enough for me to realise what was going on, even though I was very small. Everything became clear. And I forgot to say that as we were being taken away from the village, there was cattle to the left of the road, and I saw a woman. When I first looked she didn't seem familiar, but then I looked again and I realised that it was my grandmother, or rather my mother's mother. She was still alive then, at least to the extent that I could see. I couldn't linger for long enough to be sure, but she was lying on the ground. And then we walked on. They continued to take us away from the village. That's what I forgot to say a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And where were you taken to subsequently?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: They were taking us to that field that I told you about a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And were you taken to that field by those Muslim soldiers you referred to?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Muslim soldier who took us out of the village, that soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And who did you meet at that field besides yourself? Was your grandmother also with you?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My grandmother was brought there with me to that field.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And do you recall any other names of ...

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remembered Cana, Micana, Stojanka, an old woman who has since died, Mara, and Cane's mother. It was a mistake that I made. It wasn't actually Cane's wife; it was Cane's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Cana, where did he come from, from what place, what village?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember right now. I may have said it earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you tell me something about the state of health of this Cana?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: How should I put it? He was a handicapped person. There was something wrong with his leg. He had a bad leg, I think it was the left leg, and his arm, too, was sort of limp like his leg. He did not seem to be in good health.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I lead the question to the village where he -- where this Cana comes from?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it correct that this Cana comes from a place called Pribidol?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. I'm not exactly familiar with those.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: To what village did you and those other persons who were captured go to?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: We passed Mount Gradina. There was a lot of shooting. We were taken through woods and across creeks to a village that I later learned was called Radijevici. I was told later on that that was what the village we were brought to was called. We were supposed to spend the night there, all of us who had been arrested. The escort consisted of one soldier only who brought us to that village. That same night they let me fire a rifle. My grandmother was frightened, but I told her not to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And where did you finally arrive, in what village?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: You mean after Radijevici?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I think the name of the next village was Kragljivoda. We suddenly emerged out of a shrubbery and reached this village called Kragljivoda.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And your final destination you did, what town was that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: The town was Srebrenica. From Kragljivoda we were taken on a lorry to Srebrenica, straight from one place to the other, to the old police station, the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And how do you know that the name of that old building is the old police station or the SUP? You were there before or did you find out later?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I found out later. And also I read it on a plaque that it was a police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And so you were taken to that old police station. Were you taken into the building? Can you tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: They took us into the building, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: To what room?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I was put in the same room as the women, separately, and there was another room where the men were. And I was left in the same room with the women.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Was that on the basement or the first floor or I don't know? Can you tell the Court.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: On the first floor. Have you been interrogated on that first day of arrival?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, not the first day. Later there were interrogations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you stay the night in that old police station?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What happened the next morning? Can you tell the Court please.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: The next morning he must have obtained permission. The man who was missing one arm came to take me to a flat where he fed me. I spent the night at his place and I spent several days with that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now I have to stop you. Thank you. I have to stop you there because I go back again -- I take you back again to that police station where you spent the night. Could you notice whether or not there were any guards in that old police station?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. There were guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How did they look like? Did they wear uniforms or military clothes or civilian? Can you please describe for the Court.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, depending, there were guards with uniforms and those wearing civilian clothes, both kinds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were these guards armed?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: With what, can you tell -- did you notice?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Rifles. I can't remember the type, but they were armed. I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And how did they treat you at the police station?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: They treated me quite well. I was not insulted or beaten, nothing like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were you -- but you were not free to go? You were detained there or free to go?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was detained there. After the first evening when I was brought there, I was not free to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, the next morning, as you told the Court, upon military authorisation you were brought to a flat. What gave that military authorisation?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: This is something that I don't know. I wasn't told. But probably that man would not have been allowed to take me away had he not obtained some sort of authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So you were taken to a flat with that man, and you spent several nights over there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters didn't get the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please repeat your answer. Speak into the microphones because the interpreters couldn't hear you. Yeah, usher, perhaps you could move the microphones a little bit nearer, if it is possible. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The question was, and I repeat: So you were taken to a flat with that man and you spent several nights over there?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: At his house. Did you spend the rest of your time at that flat or were you subsequently taken to another place?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What kind of place, please tell the Court?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: After that, I was taken to this restaurant -- some sort of restaurant. I'm not sure what it was called. That's where I was taken. Later I would stay with the lady cooks there. I slept at the flat of one of these lady cooks. I shared the flat with her and her family.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, can you please tell me what kind of restaurant that was. Was that a common place for everybody to go or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believed at the time that this was a place where the military took their breakfast and lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You mean that this was a place where Muslim soldiers came to eat or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And were you interrogated during that time when you stayed in the restaurant and the flat of the cook?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No. I was interrogated later when we were in the flat of that neighbour whose name, as they said, was Mandza. He asked me things about the Serbian army and whether my father was armed, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will get back to that issue later on. You speak about this person. Earlier you spoke about the person -- the Muslim soldier who captured you and who was referred to as being Naser Oric. Did you after your arrival in Srebrenica meet this person again, this person referred to as Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: While I was staying in that restaurant, a man came over and sat down. There was some sort of the bar or a trestle. He pointed his finger at me. He was facing away from us, but the man pointed his finger at him and said, This is Naser Oric. He is the main man around here. I can't say -- he did look like that man, but I can't be sure that it was him. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. But while he was there he asked one of the lady cooks whether this was the young boy that had been arrested, and she said, Yes. As the two of them were talking, I heard Naser using the very same words saying, No one is to touch this young lad, this is something that I heard, and this person looked very much like the man from before but I was not entirely sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So you stayed over there in the restaurant. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I spent quite a number of days there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you visit beside that restaurant, that military restaurant, also other buildings --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't think he agreed it was a military restaurant. He said how soldiers would sometimes come and have breakfast and lunch, so I would object to that characterisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it's a characterisation; it's probably Mr. Wubben's English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Could be, but can he just refer to the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Point taken. You don't need to worry about, Mr. Wubben. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were you taken to another building in Srebrenica, apart from that restaurant where the military came to eat?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was taken to the hospital and to the prison. I would be taken to the prison almost on a daily basis when the cooks brought the prisoners food, breakfast or lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And the cook who brought the food to the prison, was that the cook you stayed with?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Depending. It wasn't always that one, but very often she was the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And that was on a daily basis during your stay in Srebrenica, that you visited --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Going there, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever I was in the restaurant, almost every single time, I went to see my grandmother.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you tell me where that prison building is in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: It's just behind the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Judges how this prison looked like, the interior of it, upon entering. What do you see?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I -- Mr. Wubben, to help you and to get over this quicker, if you have got anything, either video or photos, to show him perhaps we can go through it faster. Because I don't think this is something that there are contentions about. You know, I mean. It's -- so if we could show him either a video that you have or photos, he would recognise the place, and that would be it and we could move.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you agree with it. Because if you have some other reason why you are asking -- then obviously I will let you ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It will limit the questions. The purpose was not a direct refreshment from looking at the video but upon his own recollection and words. But I'm able now to limit my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So you paid a visit frequently to your grandmother?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you described the -- where your grandmother was in the prison. She was in a cellar, a room? Can you please tell the Court.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she was in a room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How did the room look like?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: It was more like a cell. It was a room in actual fact, but it looked very much like -- I'm not sure how I should put it. It wasn't quite finished in a manner of speaking or decorated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were there beds, chairs?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Only mattresses. There was a stove there that they were given for heating.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How was your grandmother doing in that room, that cell?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I think it was fine. Whenever I came, she never complained that anyone had touched her or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were you able to visit that cell on arrival in the prison, to go into the cell?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Every time the meals were brought, I was allowed to enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So you were more or less free to go in the prison?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but not all over the place. Around that room, yes, I was allowed to enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you also notice a toilet?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you describe what you saw?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: It was quite untidy. The tiles were in pieces. Quite untidy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And were there more than one toilet?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I only saw that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What can you tell the Court about guards? Were there any guards, and, if so, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: There were guards, like I said before. Sometimes they would be dressed in civilian clothes and sometimes they would be wearing camouflage uniforms, the military uniforms, the green kind, same thing as before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And how did the guards treat the female prisoners, did you notice?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: At least to the extent that I noticed, they were not very strict with them. I did notice once that a girl ended up on a stretcher, which probably meant that a guard had slapped her, which would seem to imply that there was more severe treatment meted out to these female prisoners as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well, please, there's no need for speculation. I just asked you what you noticed. It's a notice -- notification. Besides these female prisoners, were there also male prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were they also put into a cell or a room?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Where was this cell or room? Was that close to the female room for the female prisoners were?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: At the end of the hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: At the end of a hall. How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: The door was straight down the corridor. There was a room, one to the left and one to the right. And this door was at the end of the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Have you been able to take a look in that cell as well, in the cell of the male prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: It did happen a couple of times that I could look, but I was not really allowed, like, in that other room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what did you see when you took a look into that cell when you were able to do so?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: There were quite a number of men there in a poor state. They were lying on the floor on blankets. That's what it was like. They were a sorry sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You tell a number of -- quite a number of. Can you give an estimation to what extent -- how many men you saw?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: It's difficult to say exactly. I can't be certain about it now. I couldn't commit myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But roughly. If you don't remember with exact precision, it doesn't matter. But a rough estimate. Were there more than ten or less than ten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thereabouts. I would say 15 and upwards, but there were certainly 15 men there, that's as least as much as I can remember now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does that explain it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you also witness how the guards treated the male prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was able to see several times. I looked on as they were beating them. That was at least what I saw how the guards treated them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How many times did you witness any beatings of those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe two or three times, possibly more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And where did those beatings take place or those -- of those male prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: It was out in the hall, just outside that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Earlier you referred to a hall or a corridor. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, you leave the room and you have the hall right there, just next to the door, if you know what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. My question now is: There is a corridor and a hall. Where did the beatings in effect took place?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: In that hall just outside the room. They would take people out of the room and start beating them right there, close to the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Sorry. Could you repeat then again. Because just outside the room, as you told the Court, there was a corridor. And at the end of the corridor there was this room of the male prisoners. That means that outside the door of the male prisoners, there's still the corridor. Let's revisit that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I told you before and if you have either a video or photos, go straight to them because we would have spared this. As I suspect that we are having interpretation -- in the sense that we are being told it's a hall when in actual fact it's a hallway or a corridor that is meant. But I don't know, because although I know a few words of the witness's language, I don't know it all. So I can't really -- and I wasn't following him in his own language. When you saw these things happening with these -- to these male prisoners, where did you see these things happening, in which part of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a moment ago it was a corridor, a hallway. At the end of the hallway, there was a room where the men were, the men's cell. So it was a corridor or a hallway. At the end of the hallway there was the men's cell. They would just take them outside of the cell. They wouldn't take them anywhere else. Just outside of the men's cell they would be beaten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think that explains it as I suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So they were beaten outside the cell. By who were they beaten if you know -- sorry. By who were they beaten --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, by the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: The guards beat them, but also sometimes I cannot say precisely who these men were, but I know they worked there as guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And how did they beat them?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: With wooden clubs that looked like baseball bats, with bars, with their hands, with their feet, whatever was convenient.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And how long did those beatings last?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes they would last for 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And were they beaten up one person by one person or several persons at the same time?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: It depended from time to time. Sometimes they would beat one man alone, sometimes they would beat several men at the same time, taking them out in groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What was the reactions of those male prisoners while they were beaten up?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: They moaned, they shrieked, they cried.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you notice also the consequences of these beatings to the bodies of -- or faces of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I could see that perfectly well, I could see the wounds, injuries, blood, bruises.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And were you able also to identify the name of one or more prisoners who were beaten up like that?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There is a man I still know and see today. His name is Ilija. His home village is Cosici. I singled him out because he was frequently taken out alone. He was beaten frequently. I don't know if there was a particular reason for it, but anyway I remarked upon him and I remember him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, let me clear this up, I think, at this stage. You told us before that you were taken together with these cooks to the prison several times, that you went with them several times. Would this be once a day or more than once a day? And if it's -- let's answer that question first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean in one day how many times we would go to the prison?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometimes we would go twice a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And would that be during the day or also during the evening or during the night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Always by day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: For how long did you stay in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: 21 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what did you notice about the men being in charge in Srebrenica? Who were in charge in Srebrenica? Did you notice any names or persons?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I would often see and hear Muslim people talking. I understood from their conversations that it was Naser and a man named Mandza. And just before my exchange, I found out there was also a Zulfo Tursun as I learned later. At the time I only heard his name as Zulfo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Earlier this morning you spoke already about this person called Mandza with a view to any interrogation. Can you tell the Court about him.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean what he looked like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No. About this person. He interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. While I was staying at his apartment -- in fact, the people who brought me to his apartment said that that was his name, Mandza.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what was his function being in charge in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. But I know that people said that -- I don't know which way to put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recall that he put questions to you in the field of interrogation?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Do I remember if he asked me questions then? Yes, he asked me questions while we were at his apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Regarding what issues?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: He asked me questions about the Serb army, about my dad --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've covered this already, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, only that this person called Mandza interrogated him, he confirmed in the earlier stage. And then I moved to another area adding to it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. If you look at the transcript you will find that he has already said that this Mandza asked him about the Serbian army and about his father, whether he was a soldier and -- he's already said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Also, Your Honour, the witness keeps saying he was asked questions. Mr. Wubben insists on being interrogated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And this was a 7-year-old boy being interrogated, you know? I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: About this other person Zulfo, what can you tell me about him, Zulfo Tursun?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Zulfo Tursun I saw for the first time when the exchange took place. Outside the prison there were men, and I realised who Zulfo was, I realised which one was Zulfo. Zulfo was teasing this man called Cana, that he would not be exchanged because he had attempted an escape before. Cana indeed escaped from the prison once before and was caught and taken back. But on that occasion, on the exchange day, Zulfo was telling Cana that he would be punished by not being exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, this Zulfo, what was his function? Why was he in charge in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm not sure he said Zulfo was in charge. Again, we are talking about this 7-year-old boy. I don't see where Mr. Wubben is getting this idea that a 7-year-old boy knew who was in charge of Srebrenica, or knew that Zulfo was in charge. Without any more background, we're entering into the realms of total speculation on the part of a 7-year-old.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can find out whether or not it is speculation. Someone can learn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's stop arguing, Mr. Wubben and Mr. Jones. Mr. Mitrovic, in your opinion from what you could see, not speculating, can you tell us what kind of a role this Zulfo was filling -- was fulfilling or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without speculating, I cannot affirm that he had a specific role or what role he was playing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did he behave in a way which to you showed at the time that he was an authority there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he displayed certain signs of -- he displayed certain signs that could leave the impression that he was somebody around there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And who else, apart from him, displayed such signs of authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what I noticed on that day, it was just Zulfo. In addition to that, there was Naser Oric. The time when I saw him in that canteen, the restaurant, when he said that nobody must touch me. And the fact that the cooks said that he was the main man around there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that gentleman was the one who said that nobody must lay their hand on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this Mandza, was he a man who showed signs of authority or not in your opinion? And I don't want speculation. I want your assessment at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, yes. He was a man of authority there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Speaking about an exchange, had your grandmother been involved in any exchange?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: My grandmother was released before I was. More precisely, she was not exactly released. She was given an envelope that she was to take somewhere. And after handing in that envelope to whomever, she was told strictly that she must return to Srebrenica otherwise I would not be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did she return to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, she did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And subsequently you were told to be exchanged as well?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What happened? When did the exchange take place?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: The day before I was transferred to the prison where I spent that night. And as far as I could understand from the talk among the guards, it was not yet certain that the exchange would take place the next day. However, the next morning when we got up we were taken outside. And the procedure began, the preparations for the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Next question: So you were taken into the prison?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean. I said we spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Was that prison behind the court building?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: How long did you stay -- how many nights did you stay there? Was it only one night or longer?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was one night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And please tell what happened the following morning with a view to that exchange.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: They woke us up, took us outside to the yard, a former parking lot as far as I understood. There were the wives of Cana and Mican present there because Mican was not quite all right. The men that had been badly beaten were not taken out. And from the talk among the people there, I understood who Zulfo was. And that's where and when we were told that the exchange would take place on that day. Until then, it was yet uncertain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You noticed that Cana was not quite all right. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, what should I tell you? You could tell by looking about him that he was not in possession of his mental capacities and he was not physically all right either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what did you find out about this person earlier referred to by you as Ilija was beaten up?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I found out from the women's talk that he had been released before me. It's not rumours; it's things that I've heard from the old women talking about among themselves. And in addition to that, I didn't see him in the last two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So where did the exchange take place?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: In a place called Vitez overlooking Srebrenica, halfway between Srebrenica and Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you meet your family back again?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, after the exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you also meet this person -- this Muslim soldier who captured you being named -- or referred to as Naser Oric after your exchange?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Did I meet Naser Oric after the exchange? You mean after everything was over? Well, I didn't meet up with him personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you ever saw a photograph or picture or a video later on in the media?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw his picture in some newspapers, and I saw him on a videotape at a friend's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And was this person that you saw referred to as Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the person. That's the man whose picture I saw in the newspaper and on the videotape. I don't know who made the recording, but he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did he look the same person as the person who captured you?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I said it looked very much like the person who captured us, but I also said that I couldn't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you also notice pictures or videos in the media referring to the ICTY, the Tribunal here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I read some sort of chronicle or update concerning the Tribunal and some coverage or newspapers, and while later I watched a videotape. I didn't follow closely, but I did read something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you identify the same person referred to as Naser Oric or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't understand what that question means really. Is it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'll be dealing with it for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm staying put, but I will be dealing with it very soon, Mr. Jones. Try to answer the question. In other words, you're being referred to these photos or videos relating to the -- to this Tribunal in which it's being put to you that you saw Naser Oric, it's being put to you. Do you recognise that person? Did you recognise that person in those videos? Let me come straight to it myself. You told us in your testimony that there was more than one occasion in which you came face-to-face with a person that either told you himself that he was Naser Oric or you were told he was Naser Oric. The first time is when you were captured in the cellar of your grandmother's house. Then you met this same -- then you met another person when you were in the canteen, in the restaurant, and you were told, That man is Naser Oric. And you told us you're not hundred per cent sure that the person you saw in the restaurant was the same person that had captured you in your grandmother's home. So we may be talking of the same person; we may be talking of two persons, two different persons. Now, later on you saw several photos, you said, and you also saw videos, and now you're also telling us you also saw photos and videos relating to this Tribunal and I take it the trial of Naser Oric. You've seen all these photos. I'm asking you to compare now these photos that you have seen, the videos that you have seen showing this man that you say is Naser Oric with the person that you saw the first time in your grandmother's cellar when you were captured. Would you say that the person that captured you in your grandmother's place and the person you saw in these photos and videos are the same person or not? Just take them one by one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't tell. I couldn't tell whether it was the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And my next question is: You were told while you were in the canteen, in the restaurant in Srebrenica, That person is Naser Oric. Now, try to remember. The person that you saw in that restaurant and the face -- the person you saw in these photos and in these videos, is it the same person or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In that case, I can say it's the same person. The person I saw later in the newspapers is the person I saw in the canteen. But I cannot go as far as to say it was the same man that captured us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's it. I think we can have a break now and we'll continue afterwards. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones, we had said we will give a decision on your oral request to be permitted to file a reply. Unfortunately, one of us hasn't received the motion as of yet, so we will come back to it after the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Wubben, he's all yours again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. One question is left before I will go to Sanction for a video. Please be informed that I will not make use of photographs, so it will be the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's up to you. I mean, we never interfere in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: One question. You told the Judges that you spent the night, one night in the prison prior to your exchange. That was the prison of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. building behind the Vukovar court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In what room did you spend the night?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: The room -- can I have a minute, please, to focus on this. The room where the women were, that's where I spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Was that the same room where also -- room with the women were. Was that the same room where prior to that your grandmother was staying?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I would like to go now to Sanction and show part of the videotape. Exhibit Number P446, Your Honour. And I made a selection within this tape in various parts so we can go easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's good. Go ahead with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please start the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please, Witness, take a look at the video. Please, Witness, I have a question. Do you recognise to identify this building?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What building is this?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: This is the police station where I spent the night, the first night following my arrival in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Was this is police station you also referred to as the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's the same building where I spent the first night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We are at 2 minutes, 45 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this part of the building?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What is it --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: This is the entrance to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We arrived at 2 minutes 50 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this part?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a flight of stairs leading to the first floor, and you can see the corridor, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this part?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the reception room with the guards were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And for the record we arrived at 2 minutes, 55 seconds picture. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue. Further, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So this was the staircase leading to the first floor where you spent the night?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. 3 minutes 30 seconds for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And I didn't notice the oral answer, please. Did you recognise it as such?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. These are the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, please continue 12 minutes, 10 seconds on the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the building that I didn't recognise at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise it now?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But I do not know which specific building it is or what it housed, if you know what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it close to the prison?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Close to the prison behind the Vukovar building -- Vukovar court building --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I apologise. I rephrase the question, please. Is that building close to the Srebrenica court building?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop, please. We arrived at 12 minutes, 44 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a passage between the court and the building that I'm not familiar with. The passage leads to the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: To what prison?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: The Srebrenica prison where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Where you were. And also where your grandmother had been detained?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this picture?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. To the right you can see the court building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop. Thank you. We arrived 14 minutes, 14 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise that picture?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is outside the prison in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is there also an entrance to see for you or don't you recognise it as such?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean an entrance? I do recognise it. There must be an entrance to the prison somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the entrance to the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: For the record, we arrived 15 minutes, 23 seconds. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Where does this door leads to, if it is a door?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: To the entrance to the prison itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop, please. We arrived 16 minutes, 9 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you recognise here?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: This is outside the reception room where the guards used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did I already put the seconds? 16 minutes, 9 seconds. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop. One further. Stop. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this at 16 minutes, 51 seconds?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the reception room where the guards used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop. We arrived at 17 minutes, 25 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you recognise?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: This is a view of the corridor inside the prison building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And where would you locate the prison cell of the male prisoners, if so?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Straight down the corridor, at the end of the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And when you referred to in your testimony about the beating up of the male prisoners, where did it took place in this picture, if so?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Straight down. I'm not sure how I should explain. They would be taken out of that room to the corridor outside the room. And it was near the entrance to the lavatory next to the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this picture 18 minutes, 29 seconds?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this picture 18 minutes, 57 seconds?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the lavatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Was this the room referred to you as a toilet?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. For the record, 19 minutes, 10 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the room in which the male prisoners were kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, the picture before was the toilet, lavatory. It was on -- near this spot where the male prisoners were beaten up. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was very near, next to the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That ends my questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I just want to make sure the lectern doesn't fall off like last time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if you need a short break, we'll give you a short break.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think that's fine now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitrovic, I just want to start, just so we're absolutely clear about the passage of time since the events about which you're testifying. You were 7 years old at the time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And this was 12 years ago, so you're now 19 years old?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Isn't it right these events must seem like an eternity ago to you, like a very long time ago?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It seems to me as if a long time had gone by.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you've no doubt spoken a lot to people over the last 12 years about these events? You've told other people what happened and spoken to them about it?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. From time to time I've talked to some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would that include speaking to your grandmother about the events?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's only to be expected, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. So she's told you about what it was like for her, the experience, what she saw, what she heard, and you've told her about your experiences?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, not in great detail, but I think it is only normal that we discussed these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's absolutely normal, and there's no reproach at all. I just want to establish that. You also mentioned Ilija. I take it that's Ilija Ivanovic who you still know and you still see?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And have you also spoken to Ilija about these events in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So you've never spoken to Ilija and Ilija has told you it was terrible, I was beaten in this way or that way and that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No. Once we broached the subject but we didn't get very far. It was not really a discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: How often do you speak to Ilija or how often have you spoken to Ilija?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In which time frame are you referring? Since those events to date?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In these last, in other words, 12, 13 years. How many times have you met Ilija and spoken to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's really hard to say how many times exactly. But we did not really discuss any details of our respective experiences in Srebrenica. This is not something that we have ever done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But have you met, say, more than --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you met more than five times in these 13 years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's really difficult to say. I really can't remember how many times exactly. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, again just as a preliminary, I think it's fair to say that most people remember very little of what happened to them when they were 7 years old, apart from some vague recollections. So you'll forgive me if I appear to be testing your recollection from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have an objection. I don't know the expertise of my learned friend regarding child psychology, meaning that he can't state as an expert what a child can remember or not when it comes to certain events that become very emotional for a certain child. So the start of the question might be rephrased.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think a certain amount of common sense is permitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll soon find out, Mr. Wubben. We'll soon find out. We'll soon find out from the questions and from the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But in the beginning, Your Honour, if I may, with all due respect, there is an assumption that a 7-year-old child and, in addition, that people in general do not know very much about these kind of memories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Move with your questions, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Mr. Wubben is making a song and dance about nothing. It was really as a preliminary so the witness understands that we want to know what he recollects and not what people have told him since then, so it's just so that the witness is clear why I'm asking him certain questions. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Before you were captured on the 16th of January, 1993, you told us that a bullet nearly hit you, I think that it went between your legs or in front of you. Now, it was very dangerous in that situation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the morning. I was on the ground floor of the new house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. So there were bullets flying around. You told us there were soldiers you saw with grenades. Didn't you feel safer when you were taken out of the village and I'll use the term evacuated, because that's what we say it was, but in any event when taken out of the village, weren't you safer than when you were there?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't understand the question. What are you trying to suggest?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you feel safer after you were taken out of the village by the soldier away from the bullets and the combat action? Is that something you felt?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: You mean if I felt safe personally?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Safer when you left the village, when you were taken out.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I said when I was in that field, that soldier grabbed me and sheltered me from being hit by a bullet, anyone's bullet, in a ditch. And I was safe at that point because he was sheltering me. So of course at that point in time I did feel safer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is that the same soldier who captured you, the one who protected you in the trench?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Going back to the soldier who captured you, isn't it right that he was friendlier than it sounded from your testimony today in that he actually said, Grandma, to your mother [sic], Grandma, is anyone else with you? And he didn't actually say, You're under arrest. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He asked whether anyone was with my grandmother. I was alone in a corner at the time, and then my grandma told him that her grandson was around. And then after he took us out he told us we were under arrest. That was later.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He wasn't aggressive towards you and your grandmother, was he?
